newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: New UN envoy begins Afghan peace assessment.
newsitem.headline: New UN envoy begins Afghan peace assessment.

text.p: A new United Nations envoy arrived in Pakistan on Friday to assess U.N. peace activities in neighbouring Afghanistan, expressing optimism about the settlement of the prolonged civil war there.

Algerian diplomat Lakhdar Brahimi, special envoy of U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan, begins a short-term mission during which he will also consult interested parties in the region, including the Organisation of Islamic Conference.

"We have to be optimistic and it depends very much on the parties concerned because Afghanistan is the responsibility, in the first place, of the people of Afghanistan," the official APP news agency quoted him as telling reporters on arrival at Islamabad airport.
Afghanistan's neighbours are also concerned about the situation there and are willing to help "but we will examine the situation first," he said.

The mission of Brahimi, a former Algerian foreign minister who headed the U.N. operation in Haiti from 1994 until 1996, is to assess U.N. peacemaking activities in Afghanistan and submit his findings to the 52nd session of the U.N. General Assembly in September, U.N. sources said.
He will be assisted by the U.N. Special Mission to Afghanistan headed by German diplomat Norbert Holl.

A U.N. official said Brahimi would meet leaders of Islamic Taleban militia at the Islamic fundamentalist movement's headquarters in the southern Afghan city of Kandahar and leaders of the opposition Northern Alliance in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif.
He also plans to meet prominent political personalities of Pakistan, senior government officials and religious leaders.
Next week, Brahimi is also due to travel to Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan to meet leaders of these Central Asian republics.
